limits.note:
MODALITY: limits. Written to /Users/daichenchai/codes/github.com/research/llm-context-management/src/deepdive/sweep/limits.json (31 sources). Session WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this task started, so zero searches ran; all URLs were verified instead through the arXiv export API / arXiv HTML, Semantic Scholar batch API (citation counts fetched 2026-08-21), curl status checks, and 8 WebFetch calls (Chroma, Meta Llama 4, DeepSeek GitHub, NVIDIA blog, Anthropic, Google blog, Databricks, DeepSeek API news). Every arXiv ID resolved to the stated title via the API; no URL is guessed.

STORYLINE THE SOURCES SUPPORT: (1) Root cost is not mysterious: attention FLOPs scale n^2 (FlashAttention) and KV cache scales linearly with n times layers x KV-heads x head-dim x bytes (NVIDIA formula). Derived numbers using Llama 3 constants: 70B at 1M tokens needs ~328 GB of FP16 KV cache (0.33 MB/token) and ~2.6e18 attention-score FLOPs for one prefill; 405B ~516 GB. Jamba's table makes the same point empirically (7B vanilla Transformer = 128 GB KV at 256K). Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so every generated token re-reads that cache -> cost per output token grows with context; this is why GPT-5-class APIs default to much smaller effective budgets and why 1M tiers carry premium pricing (pricing itself belongs to the market modality). (2) Quality decays far before the nominal limit: Lost-in-the-Middle (U-curve), RULER (GPT-4 128K -> 64K effective), NoLiMa (GPT-4o effective 8K, Gemini 1.5 Pro 2M-claimed -> 2K when lexical overlap removed), Chroma context rot (18 frontier models, July 2025), and 'Context Length Alone Hurts' (13.9-85% drop even with perfect retrieval, Oct 2025). STRING explains mechanism: effective length usually < half of training length because relative-position frequencies are left-skewed. (3) Extension is a positional-encoding plus data problem: PI -> NTK-aware/YaRN -> LongRoPE(2) rescale RoPE; Llama 3 spent ~800B tokens over six stages to reach 128K; Qwen2.5-1M trained to 256K then extrapolated 4x with DCA and used synthetic long data because natural long instruction data is scarce (LongRoPE abstract names 'scarcity of long texts' as a limiting factor); Llama 4 Scout advertises 10M while trained at 256K (iRoPE). (4) Architectural routes that change the asymptote: trainable sparse attention (DeepSeek NSA 11.6x decode at 64K; DSA in V3.2 selects 2,048 KV tokens/query and enabled >50% API price cut; Kimi MoBA 6.5x at 1M prefill), local/global hybrids (Gemma 3 5:1 with 1,024 window; Mistral SWA 4,096), KV compression (DeepSeek-V2 MLA -93.3%), linear/SSM hybrids (Mamba, Jamba 4 GB KV at 256K, MiniMax-01 7:1 lightning attention to 4M, Kimi Linear -75% KV and 6x decode at 1M, Qwen3-Next Gated DeltaNet hybrid 262K native/1.01M extended), and memory modules (Titans >2M with test-time learned memory; Infini-attention 114x compression, 1M passkey with a 1B model). (5) Distributed: Ring Attention shards the sequence across devices so context scales with device count (exact, but total cost still quadratic) - it is how 1M-10M training runs exist. (6) Why ~1M is the practical plateau: Google's Feb-2024 blog states 1M was 'computationally intensive' (shipped 128K default, 1M in limited preview) and 10M was 'close to the thermal limit' of TPUs; MiniMax sized its model so 1M fits one 8-GPU 640 GB node in 8-bit; evaluation shows effective length << claimed (RULER/NoLiMa), so vendors cannot honestly market beyond what quality holds; Databricks shows most 2024 models peak at 16-64K in RAG settings; Anthropic's Sept-2025 guidance is to treat context as a finite 'attention budget' and use compaction, notes, sub-agents and just-in-time retrieval instead of bigger windows.

Extra verified URLs not given their own entry (all resolved via arXiv API/curl): ALiBi https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12409 (train 1024, extrapolate 2048, 11% faster, 1,349 cites); RoFormer/RoPE https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864 (6,179 cites); GQA https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245 (1,686 cites); RWKV https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13048 (14B dense RNN, 1,183 cites); Effective Long-Context Scaling (Llama 2 Long) https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16039 (abundant long text 'not the key'; continual pretraining cheaper than from-scratch, 355 cites); LongRoPE2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20082; Controlled Study on Long Context Extension https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12181 (approximate attention methods systematically underperform; exact fine-tuning works within range, extrapolation hard); UltraLong 128K->4M https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06214 (NVIDIA, Llama3.1-8B to 1M/2M/4M); LongBench v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15204 (503 questions up to 2M words; best model 50.1%, o1-preview 57.7%, humans 53.7%); Gated DeltaNet https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06464 (ICLR 2025, 429 cites); Gemini 2.5 report https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06261; DeepSeek-V3 https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437 (2.788M H800 GPU-hours); DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp GitHub https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp; Qwen3-Next card https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct; Mistral 7B https://mistral.ai/news/announcing-mistral-7b/.

UNKNOWNS: exact publication dates of the NVIDIA blog and Mistral 7B post were not shown in the fetched text (years given from content context); no primary-source statement from OpenAI on why GPT-5 defaults to a smaller window was gathered in this modality (search budget unavailable) - leave to the market modality.

systems.note: BUDGET NOTE: WebSearch was already exhausted session-wide (200/200) before this sweep started, so zero searches ran; all evidence comes from 8 WebFetch calls on canonical URLs plus reference lists inside those pages. File written to /Users/daichenchai/codes/github.com/research/llm-context-management/src/deepdive/sweep/systems.json (20 sources). Coverage achieved: multi-node prefill (Meta context parallelism), training sequence parallelism (DeepSpeed-Ulysses vs Megatron SP), disaggregated prefill/decode and KV offload (Mooncake, NVIDIA Dynamo), decode hardware bottleneck at 1M+ tokens (NVIDIA Helix), paging/prefix reuse (vLLM, SGLang/Dynamo radix routing), KV compression taxonomy (survey: H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM, KIVI, CacheGen, PyramidKV), and decomposition-over-window evidence (Chain-of-Agents). NOT COVERED due to budget: direct Ring Attention / Striped Attention papers, Megatron-Core context-parallel docs, LMCache, CacheBlend, MemGPT, TokenSkip, speculative decoding, and any 2026 model-window spec pages (GPT-5 default window, Claude/Gemini 1M) — the report should take those from other modalities. The four KV-compression entries with url=unknown are described only via the survey (their year field is the survey's year, not the original paper's). The Mooncake fetch mislabeled vLLM's arXiv ID (it gave the LLaMA-2 ID), which is why vLLM was fetched directly. SYSTEMS SYNTHESIS: (1) Prefill at 1M tokens is feasible but expensive: 77s on 128 H100s for a 405B model, i.e., roughly 2.7 GPU-hours per single 1M-token request, which is the TTFT/cost wall that makes providers cap or price long windows. (2) Decode at multi-million contexts is bounded by HBM bandwidth for streaming the KV history every step, not by FLOPs (Helix), so per-token latency degrades with context even when memory fits. (3) KV memory grows linearly per token x layers x heads (survey formula), so serving stacks page it (vLLM), share prefixes (RadixAttention, Dynamo router), spill it to DRAM/SSD/object storage over RDMA/NIXL (Mooncake, Dynamo), split prefill from decode onto different GPU pools (Mooncake +75% requests in production; Dynamo up to 30x on GB200 NVL72 for R1), chunk prefill (Sarathi), and compress/evict/quantize (H2O, SnapKV, KIVI). (4) The non-window answer has direct evidence: Chain-of-Agents with 8k-token workers beat both RAG and 200k full-context baselines on eight datasets, with ~100% gains above 400k input tokens, suggesting that beyond a few hundred thousand tokens, distributing the problem across agents can outperform widening the window.

writer.title: Deep dive: why context windows stop near 1M — and how to push past it
writer.takeaway: 1M is an economic and quality ceiling, not a physical one: attention compute is quadratic, KV cache is ~0.33 MB/token on Llama 3 70B (328 GB at 1M), and independent benchmarks put effective context one to three orders of magnitude below nominal (GPT-4.1 1M → 16K, Llama 4 Scout 10M → 1K on NoLiMa). GPT's "~275K" was GPT-5's 400K window minus a 128K output reservation; GPT-5.6 Sol now lists 1.05M at 3.2x the input price. Distributed serving (context parallelism, disaggregated prefill/decode, networked KV pools) removes the memory wall but not the quadratic work, the per-token bill, or the quality decay; for those, distribute the problem via retrieval, compaction and sub-agents.

kv_models.note: 2 x 32 x 32 x 128 x 2 = 524,288 B/token (0.5 MB). NVIDIA's worked example: ~2 GB at 4,096 tokens; 524 GB at 1M. Jamba Table 1 independently reports 128 GB at 256K for LLaMA-2 7B.
2 x 80 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 327,680 B/token (0.33 MB); 328 GB at 1M tokens, more than four 80 GB H100s before weights. Architecture from Llama 3 paper (80 layers, 8 KV heads, dim 8192/64 heads).
2 x 126 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 516,096 B/token; 516 GB at 1M. Magic's estimate: 638 H100s to hold one 100M-token cache for Llama 3.1 405B (magic.dev).
2 x 28 x 4 x 128 x 2 = 57,344 B/token; 57 GB at 1M, consistent with Qwen's stated >=120 GB total VRAM to serve 1M (weights + KV + activations). head_dim = 3584/28.

MLA caches one latent per layer: 61 x (kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64) x 2 B = 70,272 B/token, no factor 2 because the latent serves both K and V; 70 GB at 1M. Full KV for its 128 heads x 128 dim would be 3,997,696 B/token (57x more). DeepSeek-V2 paper reports 93.3% KV reduction vs DeepSeek 67B.

causes.cause: Attention compute is quadratic in length
causes.effect: Prefill time and time-to-first-token grow superlinearly
causes.evidence: 1M-token prefill of Llama 3 405B takes 77 s on 128 H100s vs 3.8 s at 128K (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01783); asymptote stated in FlashAttention (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135); Google: 10M tokens 'close to the thermal limit' of TPUs (https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/long-context-window-ai-models/)

causes.cause: KV cache grows linearly per token
causes.effect: One 1M request exhausts multi-GPU HBM; batch size collapses
causes.evidence: Llama 3 70B: 2x80x8x128x2 B = 0.33 MB/token, 328 GB at 1M (architecture https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.21783; formula https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/mastering-llm-techniques-inference-optimization/); Jamba Table 1: 128 GB KV for LLaMA-2 7B at 256K (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19887)

causes.cause: Decode streams the whole KV history
causes.effect: Token latency rises and concurrency falls as context grows
causes.evidence: Helix analysis: each generated token must stream the full KV cache from DRAM plus FFN weights (https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/asking-an-encyclopedia-sized-question-how-to-make-the-world-smarter-with-multi-million-token-real-time-inference/); decode is memory-bound (https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/mastering-llm-techniques-inference-optimization/)

causes.effect: Effective length stays at or below half the trained length
causes.evidence: Left-skewed relative-position frequency; STRING recovers >10 RULER points without training (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18745)

causes.cause: Long documents scarce; long fine-tuning costly
causes.effect: Windows stall near 128K; extrapolation substitutes for training
causes.evidence: LongRoPE names fine-tuning cost, scarce long text, catastrophic new positions (https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13753); Llama 3 spent ~800B tokens over six stages to reach 128K (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.21783); Llama 4 Scout trained at 256K, marketed 10M (https://ai.meta.com/blog/llama-4-multimodal-intelligence/)

causes.cause: Attention dilutes across distractors and length
causes.effect: Accuracy decays far below nominal window ('context rot')
causes.evidence: NoLiMa: GPT-4.1 1M claimed, 16K effective; Llama 4 Scout 10M claimed, 1K effective (https://github.com/adobe-research/NoLiMa); 18-model Context Rot study (https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot); 13.9-85% drop even with perfect retrieval (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05381)

causes.effect: Economic ceiling: builders avoid prompts above 200K
causes.evidence: Gemini 2.5 Pro $1.25 -> $2.50 input above 200K (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing); all Grok models 2x at >=200K (https://docs.x.ai/docs/models); OpenAI's 1.05M GPT-5.6 Sol at $4 vs 400K GPT-5 at $1.25 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol)

writer.distributed_answer: Partly. A distributed system solves the capacity half of the bottleneck: context parallelism (Ring Attention; Meta's pass-KV/pass-Q) spreads one sequence's attention across GPUs so length scales linearly with device count, and disaggregated serving with a networked KV pool (Mooncake, NVIDIA Dynamo) moves the cache off HBM into DRAM, SSD and object storage. Meta prefills 1M tokens of Llama 3 405B in 77 s on 128 H100s at 93% efficiency. It does not solve the other half: total attention FLOPs stay quadratic, every decode step still streams the whole KV history, the customer still pays per token, and measured accuracy still decays past tens of thousands of tokens. For that, distribute the problem: chunk, retrieve, compact, and chain sub-agents.

gap.title: Google's current flagship (Gemini 3.x) window, input cap and price tiers, plus Gemini 2.5 Pro's exact input limit
gap.why: The section names Gemini 3 twice but its only Google rows are Gemini 2.5 (2025 models) whose per-model input limit was never fetched; the claim that every major vendor sits at 1M as of 2026-08-21 therefore rests on a stale row, and the 2x-above-200K price-cliff argument should be confirmed against Google's current model.
queries: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models Gemini 3 Pro input token limit output token limit
Gemini 3 Pro pricing per 1M input tokens prompts above 200K tokens
Gemini 3 Pro long-context benchmark MRCR OR NoLiMa OR RULER results

critic.notes: Arithmetic verified by script: Llama 2 7B 524,288 B/token (2.15 GB at 4K, 128 GiB at 256K matches Jamba Table 1); Llama 3 70B 327,680 B/token = 327.7 GB at 1M (> 4 x 80 GB); Llama 3 405B 516,096; Qwen2.5-7B-1M 57,344 (head_dim 3584/28 = 128); DeepSeek-V3 MLA 61 x 576 x 2 = 70,272 with full-KV 3,997,696 (56.9x); 922K + 128K = 1.05M; 4/1.25 = 3.2x; GQA 8x (70B) / 16x (405B); 77 s vs 3.8 s is 20x time for 7.8x tokens (superlinear as claimed). GPT 'default' section correctly separates fetched facts from labelled inference, and flags the 272K split as arithmetic. Distributed-systems reasoning is sound (context parallelism spreads attention FLOPs/KV, decode still streams full history, quality curve unchanged, multi-agent distributes the problem); only the KV-offload bandwidth trade was missing. All model prices in the table match the structured sweep data and carry a 2026-08-21 date except GPT-4.1 (price unknown, noted) and open-weight rows (no price). Secondary unresolved item not chosen as the gap: ChatGPT per-plan context limits (HTTP 403) remain unverified and the section already says so. Could not verify from memory alone: the NoLiMa '11 of 13 models below half at 32K' count (earlier NoLiMa versions said 10 of 12), Mooncake's 800 Gbps and ~50% hit-ratio figures, and the Feb 2026 date for OpenAI auto-compaction; all are left as stated.

gapSection.title: Addendum: Google's current window, verified against Gemini 3.x
gapSection.takeaway: Fetched 2026-08-21: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (Feb 2026), Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 2026) and Gemini 2.5 Pro all list 1,048,576 input / 65,536 output tokens, so the "every major vendor at 1M" claim now rests on current Google rows; the 2x-above-200K input cliff is confirmed for the Pro line ($2.00 to $4.00 on 3.1 Pro, $1.25 to $2.50 on 2.5 Pro; output 1.5x) but absent on all Flash models; and Google's own MRCR v2 card shows 84.9% at 128K dropping to 26.3% at 1M for 3.1 Pro (unchanged from Gemini 3 Pro at 1M) — the first vendor-published Gemini 3 figure at the full window, though no independent suite covers Gemini 3 yet.
gapSection.notes: Session WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this task, so 0 of the 4 queries ran as searches; all URLs were obtained from WebFetch results instead (the models page given in the queries, then links it exposed: per-model pages, pricing page, DeepMind model cards). 8/8 WebFetch used. Key verified numbers: gemini-3.1-pro-preview input 1,048,576 / output 65,536 (page 'latest update' Feb 2026; model card release 2026-02-19); gemini-3.7-flash 1,048,576 / 65,536 (page update Aug 2026; card release 2026-08-13; cutoff Mar 2026); gemini-2.5-pro 1,048,576 / 65,536 (update Jun 2025; cutoff Jan 2025; page revised 2026-06-23). Pricing: 3.1 Pro $2.00/$4.00 input and $12/$18 output at the 200K split, caching $0.20/$0.40, storage $4.50/M/hr, batch 50%; 2.5 Pro $1.25/$2.50 and $10/$15; 3.5 Flash $1.50/$9.00 flat; 3.6 and 3.7 Flash $0.75/$3.75 promo through 2026-12-31 then $1.50/$7.50, flat. Benchmarks (vendor cards): MRCR v2 8-needle, 3.1 Pro 84.9% at 128K avg vs Gemini 3 Pro 77.0%; 26.3% at 1M pointwise for both; 3.7 Flash 97.0% at 128K vs 3.6 Flash 91.8%, no 1M figure. Models overview page lists no 'Gemini 3 Pro' entry (3.1 Pro Preview is the current Pro) and states no per-model limits. Suggested edits to the main section: replace 2.5 Pro '1M-class' with 1,048,576, add 3.1 Pro and 3.7 Flash rows, narrow 'Google doubles above 200K' to Google's Pro line, cite 26.3% at 1M in the Confidence/quality-wall text. Unknowns: Gemini 3.5 Flash per-model limits (not fetched); no independent NoLiMa/RULER result for any Gemini 3.x. Caveat: per-model pages were read via the WebFetch summarizer; numbers are quoted as returned.
